Date: Mon, 29 Oct 2028 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: EU-only processing + temporary access for regulatory hold

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Two follow-ups from our side as we prepare for procurement: we need confirmation that HealthSys data can be processed solely within EU regions (Schrems II / SCCs compliance) and a defined process for temporary access when local regulators issue an e-discovery or audit request (we call this "temporary legal access").

Specifically:
- Can Redwood guarantee in-region compute + backups limited to EU datacenters for HS-4421?
- If regulators request a dataset, what is the approved mechanism for temporary access by our legal team? We need auditability, minimum scope, time-bound access, and an evidentiary deletion certificate after the event.
- Any additional controls (CMK, escrow, operator access attestations) you can propose would be great.

Attached is a short checklist from our LegalOps team (HealthSys_SCCs_QA.pdf). Please let me know who on your side will own each piece and an expected delivery timeline.

Best,
Marie
---
Marie Dubois
Head of Privacy & Legal Operations
HealthSys Europe

Subject: Re: EU-only processing + temporary access for regulatory hold

Marie — thanks for the clear checklist and the call. Looping in Evelyn (Product Security), Naomi (Privacy & Compliance), and Vivek (Infra) to scope deliverables.

Quick answers up front:
1) In-region compute and backups: yes — we can provision an EU-only tenant + isolated S3 buckets and lock backups to EU zones. We'll provide an attestation and configuration snapshot.
2) Temporary legal access: we propose a documented runbook that covers: customer-initiated request validation, minimum-privilege operator session (just-in-time access), CMK unwrapping policy (customer-managed key option), full audit trail (requester, scope, TTL), and post-event deletion certificate.
3) Controls: offer CMK (bring your own key) + optional escrow with an HSM-based split-key scheme for emergency access; operator access requires multi-party approval and is logged.

Action owners:
- Naomi: produce the compliance runbook & attestation template (ETA 3 business days)
- Vivek: network/routing and backup isolation diagrams + KMS configuration notes (ETA 2 business days)
- Evelyn: operator access policy & audit log proof samples (ETA 2 business days)

I'll consolidate and send to LegalOps with proposed language. If HealthSys wants a formal amendment to the DPA for temporary access, we can draft redlines.

Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Oct 2028 14:08:00 +0100
Subject: Re: EU-only processing + temporary access for regulatory hold

Marie — attaching the first draft of the runbook and the attestation template we discussed (temporary-access-runbook-v1.md attached). Highlights:
- Scope: covers service, model outputs, and customer prompt data; excludes aggregated telemetry.
- In-region enforcement: IAM policies + VPC routing and S3 configuration prevent egress from EU AZs; backups are retained only in EU buckets and encrypted with a customer-managed or Redwood-managed CMK scoped to the EU tenant.
- Temporary access workflow:
  1) HealthSys submits signed LegalOps request + regulator notice
  2) Redwood validates identity and request scope (LegalOps review)
  3) On approval, a JIT operator session is created with ephemeral keys (max TTL: 8 hours) and explicit KMS unwrap logs tied to the request ID
  4) All actions are recorded, immutable audit bundle exported to HealthSys S3 (EU-only)
  5) After the event, operator credentials are revoked and we issue a signed Deletion & Access Certificate documenting what was accessed and confirmation of removal (if any temporary copies were created).
- Evidence: sample audit export (log snippets) and attestation language included.

Open items for legal: whether HealthSys requires escrowed split-keys or will use BYOK. Also need to confirm retention window for exported audit bundles.

Naomi Feldman
Privacy & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
